summary:
Verdict: the rule values are right, but the product is not ready to sell until four major gaps are closed. I found no wrong number anywhere (tax table, CPF rates and ceilings for 2025 to 2027, SRS caps, top-up caps, retirement sums, relief amounts, deadlines). For the core buyer, a Citizen or PR under 55 using SRS and a top-up to their own CPF, the plan and its wording hold up. I found no blocker under the strict definition; the first problem below is the closest to one.

I inventoried 229 user-visible factual claims across the web page, engine warnings, rule data, workbook and READMEs: 202 are supported and 27 are flagged. The inventory is at .tmp/final-review/claims.md. official pages could only be read through search extracts.

Top problems, most serious first:
1. **Age 55 and over, top-up to own CPF.** The plan says "Put S$8,000 into your CPF" by default. From 55 the CPF Board accepts top-ups well above the Full Retirement Sum, but relief stops at it and the money cannot be taken back. The only warning is a low-key "Note" far down the page.
2. **Family top-ups and matching grants.** The first S$2,000 a year given to a parent on the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme earns no relief (S$1,000 under the MediSave scheme). The product mentions the rule without amounts and counts the full S$8,000 as relief, so the headline saving is overstated.
3. **Foreigners and SRS.** They are told "S$40,000 a year comes out tax-free". That holds only for someone taxed as a resident at withdrawal. A foreigner who has left Singapore pays at least 15% on the taxable half, so SRS dollars that save 7 cents today are a net loss.
4. **The workbook says less than the free web page.** It never says that a matched top-up earns no relief, never gives the S$8,000 income test for a spouse or sibling, and has none of the "Before you transfer" facts.

The rest are minor wording and consistency points: the CPF Board given a 7pm cut-off, "guaranteed" interest, "never a wasted dollar", the lock-in age on the Rules sheet, commissions, the Basic Healthcare Sum after 65, and a README link to a file that is not in release/.

Disclosures are otherwise in good shape. The disclaimer is on the web page, the workbook and the README. 2027 is labelled as a projection wherever it can be chosen on the web page. Nothing implies endorsement by IRAS or the CPF Board.

findings.where: src/engine/warnings.ts:251-265 (AGE_55_PLUS_TOPUP, severity 'info'); src/web/App.tsx:149-151 (not among the notices shown above the plan); src/web/components/Inputs.tsx:402; workbook/sheets/planner.ts:328-338; workbook/sheets/working.ts:805-810
findings.claim_or_behaviour: For a user aged 55 or over, the top-up to own CPF is on by default and a blank "Room left in your CPF accounts" is read as unlimited (web hint: "Leave empty if the limits are far off"; workbook: "Blank = plenty of room"). The headline says "Put S$8,000 into your CPF". The only caution is an info-level "Note" under Before you transfer: "From age 55, cash top-ups go to your Retirement Account and earn tax relief only up to the Full Retirement Sum (S$220,400 in 2026). Check your balance and enter the room you have left."
findings.what_is_true: From 55 the CPF Board accepts cash top-ups to the Retirement Account up to the current Enhanced Retirement Sum (S$440,800 in 2026). Relief is given only on the current Full Retirement Sum (S$220,400) less Retirement Account savings, which exclude interest and government grants. IRAS's own worked example gives no relief where the account is already at the Full Retirement Sum. The top-up cannot be reversed. Below 55 the Special Account cannot be topped up past the Full Retirement Sum at all, so there the risk is only a wrong figure. Sources: IRAS, "Central Provident Fund (CPF) Cash Top-up Relief", https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/central-provident-fund-(cpf)-cash-top-up-relief ; CPF Board, "How much tax relief can I enjoy when I make cash top-ups?", https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-much-tax-relief-can-i-enjoy-when-i-make-cash-top-ups . Verified in this audit from search extracts of both pages.
findings.consequence: Citizen who turns 55 in 2026, S$12,000 a month plus S$30,000 bonus, S$5,000 other reliefs, Retirement Account formed with the full S$220,400. The tool says SRS S$15,300 plus own CPF S$8,000, saving S$3,495 (engine run). The real saving is S$2,295. The S$8,000 is accepted by CPF, earns no relief (S$1,200 of promised saving never arrives) and is locked for good. Someone who turned 55 in 2025 has about S$7,400 of room, so S$600 of an S$8,000 top-up earns nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: 1) Raise AGE_55_PLUS_TOPUP to 'caution' and add its code to the top-notice filter in App.tsx. 2) Reword it: "From age 55 the CPF Board will accept a cash top-up up to the Enhanced Retirement Sum, but only the part up to the Full Retirement Sum (S$220,400 in 2026) earns tax relief, and a top-up cannot be reversed. Your CPF Retirement dashboard shows how much you can still top up with relief. Enter it under 'Room left in your CPF accounts'. Until you do, this plan assumes the whole S$8,000 qualifies." 3) Better, as a model change: when age is 55 or over and the room field is blank, recommend S$0 to own CPF and ask for the figure. Make the same change to the workbook note at planner.ts:335.

findings.where: src/web/text.ts:392, 447-450, 487; src/web/components/Inputs.tsx:413; workbook/sheets/planner.ts:339-348; SPEC.md section 5.4 ("No relief for" row)
findings.claim_or_behaviour: "Up to S$8,000 across all family members." and "Relief on up to S$8,000 a year for parents, grandparents and some spouses or siblings." The only caveat is "A top-up that attracts a government matching grant earns no tax relief." No amount is given, nothing says who is affected, and there is no input for it. The plan counts every family dollar up to S$8,000 as relief.
findings.what_is_true: Matched Retirement Savings Scheme: for Singapore Citizens aged 55 or over with retirement savings below the Basic Retirement Sum (S$110,200 in 2026), and from 2026 eligible persons with disabilities of any age, the Government matches the first S$2,000 of cash top-ups a year (lifetime S$20,000). That matched S$2,000 earns the giver no relief from YA2026. CPF's own example: S$3,000 to an eligible recipient gives S$1,000 of relief. Matched MediSave Scheme: up to S$1,000 a year, no relief from YA2027. These recipients are exactly the low-balance parents that children top up. Sources: CPF Board, "How much tax relief can I enjoy when I make cash top-ups?", https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-much-tax-relief-can-i-enjoy-when-i-make-cash-top-ups ; CPF Board, "Matched Retirement Savings Scheme: what you need to know", https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/infohub/educational-resources/matched-retirement-savings-scheme-what-you-need-to-know ; IRAS CPF Cash Top-up Relief page. Verified in this audit by search. The research log had the S$2,000 and S$1,000 figures at medium confidence but they never reached the product.
findings.consequence: The opening example (age 35, S$10,000 a month, S$15,000 bonus) with family top-ups switched on, giving S$4,000 to each of two parents on the matching scheme. The tool says the plan saves S$3,478. Only S$4,000 of the S$8,000 earns relief, so the real saving is S$3,139.50, which is S$338.50 less. A taxpayer in the 15% band is S$600 short. To earn the full S$8,000 of family relief they would have to give S$12,000.
findings.suggested_fix: Model change: add an optional field under the family top-up, "Of this, how much the Government will match (earns no relief)", and subtract it from the family relief. Minimum copy change, replacing text.ts:487 and adding to the workbook family note: "If the family member is a Singapore Citizen aged 55 or over with less than the Basic Retirement Sum (S$110,200 in 2026), the Government matches the first S$2,000 you top up to their Retirement Account each year, and for some aged 55 to 70 the first S$1,000 to MediSave. The matched part earns you no tax relief, so this plan overstates your saving by that amount times your tax rate." Add the CPF matching-grant page to the source links.

findings.where: src/web/text.ts:423-432 ("Tax later" row) and 59-64 ("Worth it (7%+)"); src/engine/warnings.ts:221-235 (FOREIGNER_NO_CPF); workbook/sheets/working.ts:792-798; SPEC.md section 5.4 ("Later tax" row)
findings.claim_or_behaviour: Shown to a user who chose Foreigner: "Half of each withdrawal is taxable. You can spread withdrawals over up to 10 years; with no other income, S$40,000 a year comes out tax-free." and "You can put up to S$35,700 a year into SRS." The default depth "Worth it (7%+)" recommends SRS dollars that save 7 cents each.
findings.what_is_true: IRAS: a non-Singaporean who no longer works and lives in Singapore is taxed as a non-resident when withdrawing from SRS. The final tax on the taxable part is 15% or the resident rates, whichever is higher. The bank withholds 24% first, or 15% if no more than S$200,000 is withdrawn in the year and there is no other income. So a foreigner or PR who has left pays at least 7.5 cents per dollar withdrawn at retirement age, and at least 20 cents per dollar on an early withdrawal (fully taxable at 15% plus the 5% penalty). The S$40,000 tax-free figure holds only for someone taxed at resident rates. Sources: IRAS, "Tax on SRS withdrawals", https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/special-tax-schemes/tax-on-srs-withdrawals ; IRAS, "Tax obligations for SRS withdrawal" (foreigners and PRs), https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/withholding-tax/withdrawal-from-supplementary-retirement-scheme-(srs)-account-(foreigners-prs)/tax-obligations-for-srs-withdrawal . Verified in this audit from search extracts, not from the pages themselves. The research file had flagged that the S$40,000 claim depends on resident rates.
findings.consequence: Employment Pass holder on S$7,000 a month plus S$10,000 bonus. The tool says put S$35,700 into SRS and save S$3,084 (engine run). S$22,700 of that saves only 7 cents per dollar (S$1,589). If he has left Singapore when he withdraws, that slice costs at least S$1,702.50 in tax, so it is locked until 64 for a net loss. The whole plan nets about S$400, not S$3,084, before any tax on growth.
findings.suggested_fix: When residency is Foreigner, replace the "Tax later" text with: "Half of each withdrawal is taxable. If you are a Singapore tax resident when you withdraw, you can spread withdrawals over up to 10 years and, with no other income, S$40,000 a year comes out tax-free. If you have left Singapore, the taxable half is taxed at 15% or the resident rates, whichever is higher, and the bank withholds tax first, so each dollar costs at least 7.5 cents to take out." Append to FOREIGNER_NO_CPF and raise it to 'caution': "If you expect to leave Singapore before you withdraw, SRS dollars that save less than about 8 cents today are not worth locking away; choose a higher minimum under 'How far down the ladder?'." Show the same sentence to PRs as a note. Add the IRAS withholding page to the source links.

findings.claim_or_behaviour: The workbook has no equivalent of the web page's "Before you transfer" facts. Its only words on family eligibility are "Cash top-ups to parents, grandparents, in-laws, or a low-income spouse or sibling." and "Choose Yes only if you have an eligible family member with a CPF account." On matching grants the Start sheet says only that it "cannot check ... that a top-up attracts no matching grant". It never says such a top-up earns no relief.
findings.what_is_true: SPEC section 5.4 and the web page state the rules the workbook leaves out. A spouse or sibling qualifies only with income of no more than S$8,000 in the year before the top-up, or a disability. In-laws means parents-in-law and grandparents-in-law only. Matched top-ups and CPF-to-CPF transfers earn no relief. The recipient's own Full Retirement Sum and Basic Healthcare Sum limits apply. SRS is locked to the retirement age in force at the first contribution (62, 63 or 64), and half of each later withdrawal is taxable. All of these are confirmed in docs/research/verify2-topup.json and verify2-srs.json; the spouse and sibling test was re-confirmed by search in this audit.
findings.consequence: A workbook buyer in the 11.5% band switches family top-ups on and gives S$8,000 to a spouse who earned S$15,000 last year. The workbook shows S$920 of tax saved. The top-up earns no relief and cannot be taken back. The free web page would have told them; the paid workbook does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a "Before you transfer" block to the Start sheet (or a ninth sheet) generated from the same lockUpFacts and eligibilityCautions text as the web page. At minimum change planner.ts:290 to "Parents, parents-in-law, grandparents and grandparents-in-law; a spouse or sibling only if they earned no more than S$8,000 last year or have a disability." and append to the family note at planner.ts:346: " No relief on any part the Government matches, or if the family member does not qualify."

findings.claim_or_behaviour: "Never recommends a wasted dollar." (README) and, beside the recommended plan on the Scenarios sheet, " Never includes a wasted dollar."
findings.what_is_true: The tool respects only the caps it knows: the S$80,000 cap, the scheme caps, the tax-free band, and the room and cash limit the user types in. It cannot see CPF balances, matching grants or whether a family member qualifies, and a blank room field is read as unlimited. A recommended top-up can therefore earn no relief (see F01 and F02, both verified by search).
findings.consequence: The 55-year-old in F01 reads "never a wasted dollar" beside a plan in which S$8,000 earns nothing. The promise is the product's headline differentiator, so an overstatement here carries more weight than elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: README and SPEC: "Never recommends a dollar that the limits it knows about would waste: the S$80,000 relief cap, each scheme's cap, the tax-free threshold, and the CPF room and cash limit you enter." Scenarios sheet: " Has no dollars above the caps. Check your CPF room and family eligibility yourself."

findings.where: src/engine/warnings.ts:304; workbook/sheets/rules.ts:145; workbook/sheets/monthly.ts:63, 89-90; workbook/sheets/working.ts:826; compare src/web/text.ts:467 and src/web/components/Sections.tsx:265-271
findings.claim_or_behaviour: Engine warning and workbook: "Banks and the CPF Board can stop taking contributions earlier" and, on the Rules sheet, "Banks and the CPF Board can stop earlier on the day (for example 7pm)." The web page says something different: "Received by the CPF Board by 31 December" and "a CPF top-up counts on the day the CPF Board receives it".
findings.what_is_true: The CPF Board says the top-up application and payment must reach it by 31 December; no earlier CPF cut-off hour was found in this audit's search or in the research log. The 7pm figure is the DBS and UOB cut-off for SRS. Source: CPF Board, "When should I submit my top-up application if I want to be eligible for tax relief in the next assessment year?", https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/when-should-i-submit-my-top-up-application-if-i-want-to-be-eligible-for-tax-relief-in-the-next-assessment-year . Verified by search for the 31 December rule; the absence of a cut-off hour is a negative finding.
findings.consequence: No money is lost because the advice errs early. But the workbook attributes a bank cut-off to the CPF Board, and two surfaces describe the same deadline differently. The real CPF risk is a slow payment method: a GIRO or cheque top-up of S$8,000 sent in the last days and received in January moves S$920 of relief (at 11.5%) to the next year.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the web wording everywhere: "Banks stop taking same-day SRS contributions before midnight on the last day, some as early as 7pm. A CPF top-up counts on the day the CPF Board receives the money, so transfer a few working days early."

findings.claim_or_behaviour: Rules sheet of the 2026 workbook: "Retirement age locked in by a first contribution this year" = 64. Planner: "Locked until retirement age". The web page gives the full rule (64, 63 or 62 by date of first contribution).
findings.what_is_true: 64 applies only to a first contribution made on or after 1 July 2026. A first contribution from 1 July 2022 to 30 June 2026 locks in 63, and an earlier one 62. Source: IRAS, "Tax on SRS withdrawals" ("64 effective from 1 Jul 2026"), confirmed in docs/research/verify2-srs.json, item retirement-age.
findings.consequence: Someone who opened an SRS account in March 2026 reads 64 on the Rules sheet; their money is free of penalty from 63. Most existing account holders are at 62 or 63, so the Rules sheet figure is wrong for them by one or two years.
findings.suggested_fix: Label: "Retirement age locked in by a first contribution made from 1 July 2026 (63 if first made 1 July 2022 to 30 June 2026; 62 if earlier)". Planner note: "Locked until the retirement age in force when you first contributed (62, 63 or 64)."

findings.claim_or_behaviour: "CPF top-ups earn a guaranteed floor rate. SRS earns 0.05% unless you invest it."; family column: "At least 4% a year, in the family member's account."; workbook: "CPF top-ups earn the CPF interest floor". The self column says it correctly: "At least 4% a year, a floor rate extended to the end of 2027."
findings.what_is_true: The 4% floor on Special, MediSave and Retirement Account money has been extended only to 31 December 2027 (CPF Board release of 22 September 2026, https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/infohub/news/news-releases/government-extends-4-per-cent-interest-rate-floor-on-special-medisave-and-retirement-account-monies-until-31-december-2027 , verified by search). After that the rate follows a formula unless the floor is extended again. The 0.05% on SRS cash is a deposit rate set by the three SRS banks, confirmed only from bank articles (research item srs-interest), not an official figure.
findings.consequence: A 35-year-old choosing "Guaranteed interest first" locks S$8,000 away for about 30 years on a promise of at least 4% that is assured for 14 months. SPEC section 11 says the copy avoids promising returns.
findings.suggested_fix: text.ts:75: "CPF top-ups earn the CPF rate: at least 4% a year until the end of 2027. SRS cash earns about 0.05% at the bank unless you invest it." text.ts:420: "At least 4% a year until the end of 2027, in the family member's account." Mirror both on the Rules sheet.

findings.claim_or_behaviour: "Voluntary contributions do not earn CPF relief."
findings.what_is_true: IRAS excludes voluntary contributions above the compulsory amount, except voluntary contributions to the MediSave Account, which earn relief under CPF Cash Top-up Relief within the S$8,000 self limit. The research marked the blanket statement "corrected" (docs/research/verify2-cpf.json, item cpf-relief-iras; IRAS, "CPF Relief for employees").
findings.consequence: An employee who paid S$3,000 into MediSave voluntarily and typed their total CPF into the override is told it earns nothing. If they then leave "Already contributed, CPF top-up to yourself" at zero, the plan recommends S$8,000 more when only S$5,000 of relief is left.
findings.suggested_fix: "Voluntary contributions to your three CPF accounts do not earn relief. A cash top-up to your MediSave or your Special or Retirement Account does: enter it under 'Already contributed' instead."

findings.claim_or_behaviour: Bonus field hint: "13th month, performance bonus, commissions." Workbook: "Bonus, 13th month, commissions and incentives, in total." The approximations note says payslips "can differ by a few dollars".
findings.what_is_true: CPF Board: Ordinary Wages are wages due wholly and exclusively for that month's employment; Additional Wages are payments at intervals of more than a month. The definition was verified by search. That a commission paid every month is therefore an Ordinary Wage, subject to the S$8,000 monthly ceiling, is my inference from the definition; the search found no CPF sentence on commissions.
findings.consequence: Salesperson on S$6,000 basic plus S$6,000 commission every month. Real employee CPF is S$19,200. Entered as the hint suggests, the tool computes S$20,400. CPF relief is S$1,200 too high and tax about S$180 too low at 15%, far more than "a few dollars".
findings.suggested_fix: Hint: "13th month, performance bonus, and commissions or incentives paid less often than monthly. Put commissions paid every month in your monthly salary."

findings.claim_or_behaviour: "MediSave: up to the Basic Healthcare Sum (S$79,000)." shown to every age. In 2027 mode the same S$79,000 appears in the hint, the facts table and the rule values; the only statement that it is the 2026 figure is one line in the assumptions list.
findings.what_is_true: The Basic Healthcare Sum is fixed for life in the year a member turns 65: S$75,500 for those who turned 65 in 2025, lower for older cohorts. S$79,000 applies to members under 65 and those turning 65 in 2026. The 2027 figure had not been published on 13 November 2026. Source: CPF Board, "What is the Basic Healthcare Sum?", https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-is-the-basic-healthcare-sum . Verified by search.
findings.consequence: A 67-year-old with S$74,000 in MediSave reads S$79,000 and enters S$5,000 of room; their real room is S$1,500 or less. CPF will not take the excess, so no money is lost, but the plan's saving is overstated by about S$3,500 times their tax rate.
findings.suggested_fix: "MediSave: up to your Basic Healthcare Sum (S$79,000 in 2026 if you are 65 or younger; if older, the figure fixed in the year you turned 65)." In a projected year add "The 2027 figure is not out yet; the 2026 figure is shown."

findings.claim_or_behaviour: SRS, who qualifies: "Age 18 or over, not an undischarged bankrupt, and a tax resident for YA2027." To foreigners: "You can put up to S$35,700 a year into SRS."
findings.what_is_true: IRAS: no SRS contribution can be made once the member has started withdrawing at or after the retirement age, or on medical grounds (verified by search, IRAS "SRS contributions", https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/special-tax-schemes/srs-contributions ). Foreigners must give their SRS bank a declaration every year for the S$35,700 cap to apply (research file verify2-srs.json, item srs-foreigner-relief).
findings.consequence: A 66-year-old still working, who began SRS withdrawals last year, is told to put in S$15,300 and save S$2,295 at 15%. The bank will refuse the contribution, so the plan's saving does not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to text.ts:456: " You cannot contribute once you have started withdrawing at or after your retirement age or on medical grounds. Foreigners must give their SRS bank a declaration each year to use the S$35,700 cap."

findings.claim_or_behaviour: Rules sheet of the 2026 workbook: "Status of these rules: final" and, beside the rebate rate, "None for this Year of Assessment."
findings.what_is_true: No Personal Income Tax Rebate has been announced for YA2027, but the YA2024 and YA2025 rebates were each announced at the Budget in February of that year, and Budget 2027 has not happened. The research marks this item "unverified" (verify2-tax.json, item pit-rebate-ya2027). The note printed just above on the same sheet says this correctly.
findings.consequence: If Budget 2027 grants a rebate like YA2025's (60% of tax, at most S$200), every tax figure is up to S$200 too high. For a low earner with S$389 of tax, the "Every tax dollar" plan's S$389 saving would shrink to S$189.
findings.suggested_fix: rules.ts:284: "None announced for this Year of Assessment. One could still be announced at the Budget in February; if so, enter the rate here and the cap below." Beside the status cell add: "final, except that a YA2027 rebate could still be announced".

findings.where: src/engine/rules/shared.ts:93-95 (shown in the web relief helper and on the workbook Rules sheet)
findings.claim_or_behaviour: Working Mother's Child Relief help: "Children born earlier: 15% / 20% / 25% of your earned income. Enter the total."
findings.what_is_true: Qualifying Child Relief plus Working Mother's Child Relief is capped at S$50,000 per child, and the total across children at 100% of the mother's earned income. Confirmed in docs/research/verify2-reliefs.json, item wmcr (IRAS, "Working Mother's Child Relief (WMCR)").
findings.consequence: Mother earning S$240,000 whose third child was born in 2022 enters 25%, which is S$60,000, plus S$4,000 child relief. Only S$50,000 is allowed for that child. Her other reliefs are S$14,000 too high and the tax shown about S$2,500 too low.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to the help text: " Child relief and this relief together cannot exceed S$50,000 for one child."

findings.claim_or_behaviour: "release/ | Ready-to-use builds: sg-tax-optimiser.html and SG-Tax-Optimiser-YA2027.xlsx" and "open release/sg-tax-optimiser.html in any browser".
findings.what_is_true: This is a repository fact, not a tax rule, and was checked by listing the folder on 13 November 2026, not from the research files. release/ contains only SG-Tax-Optimiser-YA2027.xlsx. A built page exists at dist/index.html, which is git-ignored.
findings.consequence: A buyer of the "Planner + offline" tier follows the README to a file that is not there.
findings.suggested_fix: Run npm run build:release before packaging so release/sg-tax-optimiser.html exists, or correct the README.

findings.claim_or_behaviour: On a workbook built for 2027, the Planner header reads "Year of Assessment 2028 · estimate only, not tax advice" and the banner never mentions projection. The projected label appears only on the Start sheet banner and as one "Check" line at the bottom of Things to check.
findings.what_is_true: SPEC section 5 requires 2027 to be flagged as projected everywhere it is shown. The web page does this in eight places; the workbook's main sheet does not do it at the top. No 2027 workbook is in release/ today, so this matters once one is built.
findings.consequence: A buyer of a future YA2028 workbook works on the Planner sheet without seeing that every figure is provisional unless they scroll to the checks.
findings.suggested_fix: planner.ts:58: append &IF(r_status="projected"," · PROJECTED RULES","") to the header formula.

findings.where: src/engine/rules/shared.ts:144; SPEC.md:560 against SPEC.md:61 and src/web/components/Sections.tsx:785-789
findings.claim_or_behaviour: Grandparent Caregiver Relief help: "S$3,000 for working mothers whose parent or grandparent looks after a child aged 12 or below." Separately, SPEC section 8.1 says "No network requests" while SPEC section 2 and the page itself say it requests Google Fonts.
findings.what_is_true: The relief also covers the husband's parents and grandparents, and the caregiver's income must not exceed S$8,000 (verify2-reliefs.json, item grandparent-caregiver). On the second point the page's own wording is the accurate one.
findings.consequence: A mother whose mother-in-law is the caregiver may leave out S$3,000 of relief, worth S$345 at 11.5%. The SPEC wording affects no user.
findings.suggested_fix: "S$3,000 for working mothers whose parent, parent-in-law or grandparent (not earning more than S$8,000) looks after a child aged 12 or below." In SPEC 8.1 write "No network requests other than the optional Google Fonts stylesheet".

checked_and_fine: Web page (src/web/text.ts, components, App.tsx): 84 claims inventoried, 77 supported, 7 flagged (see F01, F03, F08, F10, F11).
Engine warnings (src/engine/warnings.ts): 16 message templates inventoried, 14 supported, 2 flagged (F06, F09).
Rule data text (relief catalogue, year notes, source links, value groups): 43 inventoried, 40 supported, 3 flagged (F07, F14, F17).
Workbook (workbook/sheets/*.ts): 75 claims inventoried, 62 supported, 13 flagged (F04 to F09, F13, F16).
README.md and workbook/README.md: 11 claims inventoried, 9 supported, 2 flagged (F05, F15).

Rule values match the research verdicts and my own recall: resident tax table from YA2024, S$80,000 relief cap, Earned Income Relief 1,000 / 6,000 / 8,000, CPF wage ceilings (7,400 then 8,000 a month; 102,000 a year), CPF rates for 2025, 2026 and 2027, graduated PR rates, SRS caps 15,300 / 35,700, top-up caps 8,000 + 8,000, Full Retirement Sum 213,000 / 220,400 / 228,200, Basic Healthcare Sum 75,500 / 79,000.
The 4% CPF interest floor extended to 31 December 2027: confirmed by search (CPF Board release of 22 September 2026).
The 2027 Basic Healthcare Sum is still unpublished on 13 November 2026 (search), so using the 2026 figure with a note is the right treatment.
No Personal Income Tax Rebate for YA2026 or YA2027 was found by search, which is consistent with the tool assuming none and saying so.
The first S$2,000 a year to a recipient on the matching scheme earns no relief, and the spouse or sibling S$8,000 test uses the year before the top-up: confirmed by search (CPF Board).
MediSave top-up limit is the Basic Healthcare Sum less the MediSave balance: confirmed by search (CPF Board).
"Banks reject anything over" the SRS cap: supported (MOF says the scheme accepts only monies up to the cap).
250% donation deduction extended to 31 December 2029, the Matched MediSave exclusion from YA2027, and retirement age 64 from 1 July 2026: all confirmed in the verify2 research files.

All 16 relief catalogue amounts match the research verdicts, including the corrected points (no income test for the disability variants; the S$5,000 life insurance test counts compulsory plus voluntary CPF).
